headline: Jones is cleared. Simmons is not. The red zone still owes a touchdown.
dek: The preseason finale produced 21 first downs, 155 rush yards, and zero touchdowns; Week 1 is Denver on ESPN with Patrick Mahomes back, Josh Simmons and Chamarri Conner already ruled out, and Chris Jones cleared after a calf scare.
videoHook: They sat on Seattle for 33 minutes, ran it for 155, and still left Arrowhead in a 9–9 tie. Now Mahomes is back, the left tackle is scratched, and Sean Payton is on the other sideline on Monday night.
theEdge: ESPN FPI posts Kansas City at 58.0 percent and DraftKings hangs a 2.5-point home number on a 43.5 total, but Polymarket’s 5.7 percent Super Bowl ticket and 10.0 percent AFC ticket still price a 6-11 hangover until Mahomes finishes drives without Simmons or Conner.

storyline.lede: The 6-11 tape is closed. What Kansas City actually put on film before the real snaps start is a 9–9 possession game that won first downs and lost the paint: 353 yards, 33:12 of clock, three Harrison Butker field goals, and a red-zone offense that treated the 5-yard line like a wall. Week 1 does not care about that control. It cares whether Patrick Mahomes, returning on a short home number against Sean Payton, can turn the same downhill identity into touchdowns while Andy Reid is already without his starting left tackle and a starting safety.
body: That is the whole opener in one sentence. ESPN FPI still leans Kansas City at 58.0 percent at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium, and DraftKings has them -2.5 at a 43.5 total, which is a trench number, not a shootout number. Polymarket is colder: 5.7 percent to win Super Bowl 61 and 10.0 percent to win the AFC, a market that has not forgotten last year’s 6-11 and will not move on a preseason tie that never reached the end zone.

The injury report is the plot twist the 9–9 tape did not have to survive. Andy Reid has declared Josh Simmons and Chamarri Conner out for the Broncos, which means the first real dropback of 2026 is coming with a replacement on the blind side and a secondary that is already a body short. Chris Jones’s calf put a scare into the week — he was limited Friday — but the final report cleared him, so Steve Spagnuolo at least gets his interior closer for an old-school AFC West blood match.

Eric Bieniemy’s job this week is not clever. It is to keep Mahomes on schedule so the vacant left tackle is blocking downhill, not pass-setting in obvious third-and-long against a Payton script. Spagnuolo’s job is the mirror image: two-deep answers without Conner, Jones as the collapse piece, and enough simulated pressure to keep Denver from turning this into a 40-pass night that hunts the backup tackle and the missing safety. The Colts and a primetime home date sit in Week 2. None of that matters if Monday night becomes another field-goal slog.

lastGameReview.label: Pre Week 4 · Sat Aug 29
lastGameReview.lede: Kansas City controlled the preseason finale at Arrowhead and still could not score a touchdown. The Chiefs out-gained Seattle 353–266, won first downs 21–13, converted 9-of-17 third downs, ran for 155 yards, and held the ball for 33:12, then left with three Harrison Butker field goals (28, 24, 19) and a 9–9 tie after Jalen Milroe hit Nick Vannett from 4 yards in the third quarter and Jason Myers missed the extra point.
analysis: The box score is a possession clinic that never got paid. Twenty-one first downs and a 155–54 rush edge mean Kansas City won early downs and the line of scrimmage. Brashard Smith’s 16 carries for 72 yards were the clearest identity snap of the night: inside-zone, one cut, stay on schedule. That is how you sit on a team for 33 minutes. It is also how you get greedy in the red zone and then settle, because the scoring sequence never changed — Butker from 28, Butker from 24, Butker from 19. A 19-yard field goal is not a field-position win. It is a failed trip to the doorstep.

Garrett Nussmeier’s 22-of-34 for 198 yards and an interception is preseason tape, not a Mahomes verdict, but it still tells you what this offense looked like without a closer. Andrew Armstrong led the receivers (5 for 54) on a night with no explosive finishing play. The passing game moved the chains and then died on the paint. When the only opponent touchdown is a 4-yard dump to a tight end and the PAT fails, you should win the game. Kansas City instead kicked a 19-yarder in the fourth quarter and shook hands at 9–9.

Defensively the finale was complementary, not dominant. Seattle managed 266 yards and 4-of-11 on third down with only 54 rush yards, and R Mason Thomas chipped in a sack. That is a Spagnuolo-looking skeleton: take away the run, live with some net passing yards (212), and trust the offense to finish. The offense did not finish. Carry that into a real Monday night against Payton and the 43.5 total starts to look like a warning, not a coincidence.

takeaways.title: The run game is real enough to build a week around
takeaways.body: One hundred fifty-five rush yards and 33:12 of possession are not a mirage, even in Week 4 of the preseason. If Bieniemy is going to protect a replacement left tackle in Week 1, this is the tape he wants: early-down zone, Smith as a volume back, and third downs that stay manageable.

takeaways.title: The red zone is still a kicking operation
takeaways.body: Three field goals, including a 19-yarder, against a preseason Seattle defense is the loudest problem on the 2026 tape. Payton will take that bet every time. Touchdowns, not first downs, are the only way a 2.5-point home favorite cashes.

takeaways.title: The closer was not on the field
takeaways.body: Nussmeier’s 198 yards and pick are a control-game stat line. Monday night is Mahomes, and the bar on that comeback should stay honest: the structure from this tape can travel, the finishing from this tape cannot.

whatWorked: Early-down run identity: 155 rush yards, Brashard Smith’s 16-for-72, and a 21-first-down clock drain.
Third-down efficiency (9-of-17) that kept Seattle’s offense on the sideline.
Run defense that held Seattle to 54 rushing yards and 13 first downs.
Complementary field position that produced three Butker makes, including from 19.
whatDidnt: Red-zone finishing: 353 yards, zero offensive touchdowns, a 19-yard field goal as the last score.
Explosive passing: Nussmeier’s 198 yards came without a closer and with an interception.
Payoff on 33:12 of possession — a control game that still tied 9–9.

currentState.lede: Kansas City is 0-0 with a 6-11 hangover, a functional run tape, and a Week 1 injury report that already removed the left tackle and a starting safety. The opener is a home favorite on ESPN, not a referendum on January, but the market’s 5.7 percent championship price will not move if Monday night looks like another three-kick night.

workOn.title: Finish the Seattle red-zone tape
workOn.body: Twenty-one first downs and a 19-yard field goal is the install that matters this week. Payton will trade field goals all night. Bieniemy has to have a goal-line and 5-yard-line answer that is not Butker, or the 43.5 total becomes a trap.

workOn.title: Protect Mahomes without Josh Simmons
workOn.body: Reid ruled Simmons out. The preseason run game is now a protection plan, not just an identity. If this turns into obvious dropback on second-and-long, Denver will hunt the vacant blind side and the Mahomes comeback becomes a survival drill.

workOn.title: Replace Chamarri Conner without giving up the top
workOn.body: A starting safety is out for a Monday nighter against a Payton script that loves play-action and the deep over. Spagnuolo has to live in two-deep answers and rally-to-tackle football, not hero coverage from a body short.

workOn.title: Use a cleared Chris Jones, don’t empty him
workOn.body: The calf scare was real enough to limit him Friday; the final report cleared him. That is not a license to play him like a 70-snap every-down piece in Week 1. Win the interior, then get him off the field.

thinkAbout.title: How low is the Mahomes bar on night one?
thinkAbout.body: History on similar quarterback returns says the expectation should be structure, not fireworks. If the offense looks like the Seattle tape — first downs, no paint — that is a problem. If Mahomes is merely clean and on time, that is a win the market has not priced.

thinkAbout.title: Did cutting Esa Pole leave them with no left-tackle floor?
thinkAbout.body: Pole started down the stretch last season, hit the Washington practice squad, and the left-tackle room is now a Week 1 nightmare with Simmons already out. Signing a veteran just to sign one (D.J. Humphries is the name in the rumor mill) is not automatically the fix. The fix might be the run game and the boot.

thinkAbout.title: Is a Wild Card the honest 2026 ceiling until this roster proves otherwise?
thinkAbout.body: Chiefs fans in the Week 1 Reacts poll already see a Wild Card seed. That matches a 5.7 percent Super Bowl ticket better than any glory narrative. Beat Denver at home and the conversation can wait a week. Lose the trenches on Monday night and the 6-11 hangover is still the story.

gamePlan.lede: Monday night at Arrowhead is an AFC West blood match on a 2.5-point home number and a 43.5 total: Kansas City is a modest favorite that has to prove the Seattle run tape travels and that Mahomes can finish drives with the left tackle and a starting safety already scratched.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Styles collide in the trenches, not in space. Kansas City just ran for 155 and sat on the ball for 33 minutes; Denver, with Sean Payton scripting, will try to make this a dropback and play-action game that hunts a replacement left tackle and a secondary missing Chamarri Conner. The Chiefs’ leverage is early-down zone, a cleared Chris Jones collapsing the middle, and Spagnuolo’s simulated pressure. Denver’s leverage is the vacant blind side, the missing safety, and any series that becomes second-and-long. The low total says both staffs already know this.

keys.title: Stay in early-down run so the backup tackle is blocking downhill
keys.body: The Seattle tape is the script: inside zone, Smith as a volume piece, 21 first downs. Every designed dropback on first down is a gift to Payton. Make Denver defend the run, then boot Mahomes off the left edge instead of asking a replacement to pass-set against a wide-9 look.

keys.title: Move the pocket and take the easy throws
keys.body: Mahomes is back, but the comeback bar is structure. Play-action boots, mesh, and screens are how you keep him clean without Simmons. If Bieniemy gets stubborn about seven-step shots, the 9–9 red zone will look generous.

keys.title: Two-deep answers without Conner, Jones as the closer
keys.body: Do not play hero coverage a safety short. Cover-2 shells take away Payton’s deep over, and a cleared Jones plus zone-blitz looks can wreck max-protect. R Mason Thomas already showed a pass-rush chip in the finale; use it in spots so Jones is not the entire plan.

keys.title: Red zone is the only stat that cashes -2.5
keys.body: A 19-yard field goal lost the Seattle game as a statement. Against Denver, Butker can still win a 9–6 slog, but the market’s 43.5 and FPI’s 58.0 percent both assume Kansas City is the more functional offense. Function without touchdowns is how 6-11 starts over.

script: Open in under-center 12/21 personnel and run inside zone to the closed side so the replacement left tackle is covered up, not isolated.
Second-series play-action boot to Mahomes’ right — away from the vacant blind side — with a leaking tight end and a deep over as the alert.
On obvious passing downs, get to an RB screen before Denver can pin the edge rusher on the backup tackle.
Red-zone first down: run it again. Do not throw a 19-yard field goal on the first trip.
Defensively, first two series in a Cover-2 shell; do not give Payton a one-high look while Conner is in street clothes.
Third-and-medium: show double-A gap, drop a lineman, send a second-level rusher — Jones as the interior threat, not the only rusher.

nextGame.label: Week 1 · Mon Sep 15
nextGame.note: Season opener, 7:15 p.m., presented by T-Mobile — a short home favorite in an AFC West blood match with two starters already out.

spotlight.title: Mahomes is back. The bar should stay honest.
spotlight.body: The last tape is Nussmeier, not Mahomes. The first real snap is a comeback start on Monday night, and the historical comps say structure beats fireworks. If he is clean, on time, and finishing the Seattle red-zone tape, that is the win. If the staff asks him to cover for a vacant left tackle, the 5.7 percent ticket stays put.

spotlight.title: The blind side is already a scratch
spotlight.body: Andy Reid ruled Josh Simmons out. Esa Pole, who started down the stretch last season, is already gone. Week 1 is not the week to discover whether a replacement can pass-set for 40 dropbacks against Payton. It is the week to run and boot.

spotlight.title: Jones’s calf cleared. The snaps still matter.
spotlight.body: A limited Friday turned into a clear final report, which is the best news on the sheet. It is not a 70-snap mandate. Spagnuolo needs the interior collapse against Payton; he does not need a Week 1 calf relapse before Indianapolis.

spotlight.title: Conner is out, so the top of the defense is the tell
spotlight.body: Losing a starting safety for a Payton opener is how you get beat on play-action overs. Two-deep, rally, and tackle. If Kansas City plays one-high to generate pressure, Denver will take the shot the 9–9 tape never had to face.

spotlight.title: The run tape is the only identity they’ve actually shown
spotlight.body: Brashard Smith’s 16-for-72 and 155 team rush yards are the cleanest thing on the 2026 film. That identity is now also a protection scheme. Abandon it and the vacant tackle becomes the game.

spotlight.title: A 58 percent favorite that the championship market still doesn’t believe
spotlight.body: FPI and DraftKings say Arrowhead still matters. Polymarket’s 5.7 percent Super Bowl and 10.0 percent AFC prices say 6-11 still matters more. Only touchdowns move that.

matchups.unit: Chiefs interior run vs. Broncos front
matchups.chiefs: Under-center zone, Brashard Smith volume, 155-yard preseason identity
matchups.opponent: Payton’s early-down front, gap-sound vs. zone
matchups.note: The only tape Kansas City has that actually worked. If it travels, the backup tackle survives. If it doesn’t, the whole script collapses.

matchups.unit: Mahomes’ blind side vs. Broncos edge pressure
matchups.chiefs: Replacement LT with Josh Simmons out; boots and play-action as the real protection
matchups.opponent: Payton scripted edges and late-add rushers on obvious dropback
matchups.note: This is Denver’s clearest path. Kansas City cannot win a 40-dropback game on this injury report.

matchups.unit: Chris Jones vs. Broncos interior line
matchups.chiefs: Jones cleared after a calf scare; R Mason Thomas as a rotational chip
matchups.opponent: Max-protect and quick game to neutralize the interior
matchups.note: A healthy-enough Jones is still the best player in this trench. Manage the snaps; don’t hide him.

matchups.unit: Chiefs secondary (minus Conner) vs. Payton play-action
matchups.chiefs: Cover-2 shells, rally-to-tackle, no hero one-high
matchups.opponent: Deep overs, play-action, and the shot Payton always keeps in his pocket
matchups.note: A starting safety is out. Give Payton a single-high look and this 43.5 total is a lie.

matchups.chiefs: 21 first downs, three kicks, a 19-yard FG as the last score
matchups.opponent: A staff happy to live in a field-goal game on the road
matchups.note: Until Kansas City proves it can punch it, Denver is playing the 9–9 tape, not the 58 percent model.

matchups.unit: Spagnuolo simulated pressure vs. Payton protections
matchups.chiefs: Zone blitz, Jones interior, second-level adders
matchups.opponent: Max-pro, slide, and hot answers from a veteran play-caller
matchups.note: This is the coaching chess match. Neither side should win it on the first scripted drive; the second-half adjustments will.

xsandos.title: Early-down inside zone, closed side
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, opening script vs. Denver — keep the replacement left tackle covered up
xsandos.why: Kansas City just ran for 155 yards and held the ball 33:12 against Seattle with Brashard Smith as the volume back. Josh Simmons is out, so every first-down dropback is a gift to Sean Payton. Under-center zone to the closed side lets Eric Bieniemy put Mahomes on schedule and hides the vacant blind side inside a downhill run instead of a pass set.
xsandos.coaching: Bieniemy: zone steps, one cut, do not bounce it to the left edge. Smith has to press the LOS and finish north-south so the backup tackle is down-blocking, not chasing. Reid should stay in 12/21 until Denver proves it can stop the Seattle tape.

xsandos.title: Play-action boot away from the vacant side
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-6 after a zone run, first two series vs. Payton
xsandos.why: Simmons is scratched and Mahomes is on a comeback clock. Booting him to his right — away from the left tackle — turns the Seattle run fake into protection and gives him a simple high-low on the perimeter instead of a seven-step drop behind a replacement. Payton will have the edge set for dropback; he is slower to the naked boot if the zone fake is real.
xsandos.coaching: Mahomes: sell the mesh point, get depth, and take the leak in the flat if the end crashes. Do not reset and hunt a hero ball into two-deep. The deep over is the alert, not the first read, until the blind side proves it can survive.

xsandos.title: Mesh vs. the man look Payton will test
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-5 to 7, middle of the field, Mahomes’ first real money down
xsandos.why: A returning Mahomes does not need a 2022 shot chart on night one, and a vacant left tackle does not need a five-man protection that loses. Mesh gives him rubs, a sit, and Brashard Smith as the outlet — the same easy-offense philosophy as the 9-of-17 third-down tape, except now the closer is actually in the game. Andrew Armstrong’s 5-for-54 in the finale is the underneath target this concept was built for.
xsandos.coaching: Bieniemy: put the mesh on the hashes and tell Mahomes the checkdown is a win. No late-in-the-progressions heroics into Conner’s vacated deep middle. If Denver sits the rub, Smith is the throw, not the seam.

xsandos.title: RB screen when they pin the backup tackle
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-long or 3rd-and-medium after Denver wins a pass-rush down
xsandos.why: Payton will hunt the left edge the first time Kansas City is behind the chains. The answer is not to max-protect a replacement tackle; it is to throw the ball to Smith in space and make Denver’s rushers run to the boundary. That also keeps Mahomes from holding it, which is the entire point of a comeback opener with Simmons and Conner already out.
xsandos.coaching: Get the left side out in front of Smith — this only works if the linemen treat it like a run. Mahomes: catch, fake, and dump. Do not pump yourself into a hit. One explosive screen is worth more than another 19-yard field goal.

xsandos.title: Cover-2 shell without Conner
xsandos.situation: Early downs and any Payton play-action look, first half
xsandos.why: Chamarri Conner is out. One-high against Sean Payton on Monday night is how you donate the deep over the Seattle tape never had to cover. Two deep, five under takes away the shot, lives with the underneath completion, and asks the Chiefs to tackle — the same complementary skeleton that held Seattle to 13 first downs and 54 rush yards.
xsandos.coaching: Spagnuolo: no hero post safety. Corners squat, safeties split the hashes, and the Mike has to be right on the play-action fake or Payton will sit the tight end in the hole. Jones can still rush; the coverage does not have to.

xsandos.title: Simulated pressure with Jones as the interior lie
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-4 to 8, second half, once Payton is in obvious protection
xsandos.why: Chris Jones is cleared after the calf scare, which means Spagnuolo finally has the player who makes the fake look real. Show double-A, drop a lineman, send a second-level rusher, and force Payton to account for Jones while the replacement pieces (including R Mason Thomas as a rotational rusher off the Seattle sack) eat a one-on-one. Do this after the Cover-2 has taken away the shot, not instead of it.
xsandos.coaching: Spags: Jones is the collapse, not the every-down stunt piece — the calf is cleared, not forgotten. The dropped lineman has to occupy the throwing lane Mahomes’ counterpart wants on the hot. If the adders are late, this becomes a bust with Conner already in street clothes.

coaching.detail: Reid called it an old-school AFC West blood match, and the 43.5 total agrees. This is not a gadget night. Reid’s edge is the run-and-boot script; Payton’s edge is the vacant tackle and the missing safety. Whoever wins early downs wins the 2.5.

The OC inherits a 155-yard run tape and a left tackle already ruled out. His Week 1 grade is simple: keep Mahomes on schedule, finish the red zone the Seattle finale refused to finish, and do not ask a replacement to pass-set 40 times.
The signature zone blitz still plays with Jones cleared. The coverage behind it cannot. Two-deep first, pressure second, or Payton will throw the shot the preseason finale never tested.

coaching.topic: Harrison Butker is not the red-zone plan
coaching.detail: Three makes, including from 19, kept them in a 9–9 tie. If he is the leading scorer again on Monday night, Kansas City did not solve the only problem on the tape.

injuries.note: Starting left tackle ruled out by Andy Reid for the Week 1 opener against Denver.
Starting safety ruled out by Andy Reid for Week 1, thinning the backend against a Payton script.
Calf injury limited him Friday; the final Week 1 injury report listed him with clear status.

personnel.move: Josh Simmons scratch forces a replacement at left tackle
personnel.detail: Reid has already taken the starter off the board for Monday night. The Seattle run tape is now the protection plan; a 40-dropback script is not.

personnel.move: Esa Pole is gone, and the tackle floor went with him
personnel.detail: Pole started multiple games down the stretch last season, was cut in the 53-man trim, and landed on Washington’s practice squad. The current left-tackle room is paying for that decision with Simmons already out.

personnel.move: D.J. Humphries is not automatically the answer
personnel.detail: The tackle market will keep offering veterans. Need is not the same thing as fit; Kansas City’s cleaner Week 1 answer is still scheme (run, boot, screen) rather than a panic signing.

personnel.move: Chris Jones returns to the interior rotation
personnel.detail: Cleared after a calf scare, with R Mason Thomas already on the preseason sack sheet as a rotational chip. Use both so the calf does not become a Week 2 story.

strategies: Build the first 15 calls around under-center zone so the replacement left tackle is never isolated on first down.
Boot Mahomes to his right after the run fake; treat the vacant blind side as a direction, not a debate.
Live in Cover-2 until Conner’s absence is accounted for; do not give Payton a one-high shot in the first half.
Script two RB screens as pressure answers rather than max-protecting a backup tackle.
Red-zone first down is a run. The 19-yard field goal from the Seattle tape is banned from the call sheet.
Rotate Jones. A cleared calf is not a 70-snap calf. Win the interior in spots, then get him off the field for Indianapolis.
debates: Is a 2.5-point home favorite actually flattering a roster that just tied 9–9 without a touchdown?
Did cutting Esa Pole turn Week 1 into a self-inflicted blind-side crisis once Simmons was ruled out?
How many snaps is a ‘cleared’ Chris Jones actually worth after a calf that limited him Friday?
Should the Mahomes comeback bar be ‘don’t get hit’ or ‘finish the red zone’?
Are fans right to see a Wild Card ceiling, or is that just the 6-11 hangover talking before a ball is snapped?

runOfShow.talkTrack: Nine-nine. Three kicks. Thirty-three minutes of clock. Then Reid scratched the left tackle and a starting safety. Welcome to Week 1.
Walk the 353-yard control game: Smith’s 16-for-72, 9-of-17 on third down, and why a 19-yard field goal is the loudest play on the tape. Nussmeier is context, not the closer.
0-0 with a 6-11 hangover. Simmons out, Conner out, Jones cleared. FPI 58.0 percent, -2.5, 43.5 total, 5.7 percent on Polymarket. Honest edges only.
Reid’s scratches, the Pole cut, why Humphries is a rumor not a plan, and how the run game is now protection.
Payton will hunt the blind side and the missing safety. Script: zone, boot, screen, Cover-2, Jones as the interior lie. Red zone is the only number that cashes.
Six calls, no filler: inside zone, boot, mesh, RB screen, Cover-2, zone blitz. Name the players. Name the scratches.
Wild Card or hangover? Then point to Indianapolis on NBC in Week 2. Monday night is the only snap that matters first.
